name: Expert Agents
description: Independent expert-agent planning, grounded research, managed corpus, document, and approved acquisition tools for OpenClaw.

factory.description: Owner-only creation authority. Disabled by default. Paths and credentials are deployment settings, never tool arguments.

rootDir.description: Pre-created private 0700 root for agent repositories and operation state, outside the machinery repository.

tokenDirectory.description: Pre-created 0700 credential directory, disjoint from rootDir.

managerTokenFile.description: Private token file for a dedicated Telegram manager with Bot Management Mode enabled and no other update consumer.

libraryBucket.description: Existing approved GCS library bucket; must match the worker registration allowlist.

libraryPrefix.description: Approved GCS prefix. Each new agent receives its own descendant prefix.

openclawBin.description: Absolute path to the deployment's OpenClaw CLI.

bunBin.description: Absolute path to Bun 1.3+ for the bundled factory.

model.description: Optional deployment-approved model for newly created agents.

activationCommand.description: Optional absolute path to an owner-approved no-argument activation wrapper. It must enforce the deployment's restart protocol. At most one attempt per creation.

remoteUrlTemplate.description: Optional https://, ssh:// or file:/// remote URL containing {agentId} exactly once. The factory pushes each new agent's initial commit there and records the resolved remote.

remoteCreateCommand.description: Optional absolute path to a deployment-owned executable that creates the remote repository idempotently. It receives the agent id and the resolved remote URL as its only arguments.

authToken.description: Bearer credential for the bounded worker: either a literal string or a SecretRef the gateway resolves. Do not commit raw values.

defaultDomainId.description: Domain id supplied for worker requests that omit one. This deployment's default expert; the tenant-neutral worker routes no default domain of its own. An explicit domain_id is never overridden.
